title: ר' שמעון בן יוסי בן לקוניא

paragraphs:
R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya. (a) He belonged to Rabbi's court and was a priest: Al Ellu Mumin, 38b. Rabbah bar bar Hana said: R' Yohanan ben Elazar—see Yonatan ben Elazar—told me, “An elder lived in our neighborhood”—Rashi: he was a priest—“and his name was R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya. Never did I pass before him”—Rashi: he was the greatest of the generation. “Once I passed before him, and he said, ‘Sit, my son. This hilazon’”—Rashi: that elder had a firstborn animal with a hilazon in its eye—“‘is a permanent blemish permitting slaughter.’” Although they said that a person does not inspect his own blemishes, he may teach the law to pupils, and the pupils rule for him, and so forth.

(b) Rabbah bar bar Hana said: Yohanan ben Elazar told me that he entered a garden after R' Shimon son of R' Yose ben Lakunya, who said that he had seen R' Shimon ben Yohai eating cabbage in the seventh year; see his entry. In Shabbat 49b: R' Yonatan ben Elazar said in R' Shimon son of R' Yose ben Lakunya's name. Perhaps it should read R' Yohanan, as immediately above. (c) In Zevahim 62b, R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya asked R' Yose, “Did R' Shimon ben Yohai say …?” (d) R' Yishmael son of R' Yose visited R' Shimon son of R' Yose ben Lakunya's house. They gave him a cup, and he drank it at once. He asked him, “Does the master not hold that one who drinks …?” He answered, “They did not say this concerning your small cup, your mixed wine, and my large belly”; see his entry.

(e) In Jerusalem Berakhot, Hayah Kore, mishnah 3, and Midrash Kohelet, at “For the living know”: R' Hiyya the Great and R' Yonatan walked before R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya's bier. R' Yonatan's fringes dragged over the graves. R' Hiyya said to him, “They will say: tomorrow they come to us, and now they revile us.” The Jerusalem reading differs; see Bavli 18. In Jerusalem Ba-Kol Me'arevin and Pesahim, Ellu Devarim, halakhah 2 [the checked parallel is at 6:1:19], R' Yonatan said before R' Hiyya the Great in R' Shimon son of R' Yose ben Lakunya's name; he asked R' Shimon son of R' Yose ben Lakunya. But in that matter in Shevuot [18b discusses a different legal question]: “R' Yonatan his brother asked …”; see his entry. Perhaps “his brother” is a scribal error, and this is the R' Yonatan who was with R' Hiyya before his bier, or the foregoing R' Yonatan ben Eliezer. (f) In Esther Rabbah, at “It was contemptible in his eyes”: R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya. At the end of Rabbah, Kedoshim: “R' Shimon ben Lakunya.” From the foregoing it should read ben Yose ben Lakunya.

(g) Jerusalem Ma'asrot 3:8 [the checked edition has the passage at 3:4:4]: R' Elazar son of R' Shimon went to R' Shimon son of R' Yose ben Lakunya, his father-in-law. He mixed wine for him and he drank; he mixed and he drank. He asked, “Did you not hear from your father how many sips a person should take from a cup?” He answered, “As it is, one; with cold water, two; with hot water, three. The sages did not make their measure concerning your fine wine, your small cup, or my large belly.” In Midrash Hazit, at “Your lips drip honey”: R' Elazar son of R' Shimon asked R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya, his father-in-law. In Rabbah, Tavo, chapter 7: R' Elazar son of R' Shimon ben Yohai asked R' Shimon son of R' Yose, his father-in-law. With some variation in Yalkut, Ekev, remez 850, in Pesikta's name: R' Elazar son of R' Shimon asked R' Shimon ben Lakunya, his father-in-law; it should read ben Yose ben Lakunya. From all the foregoing, it appears that R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya was the father-in-law of R' Elazar son of R' Shimon ben Yohai.

But in Bava Metzia 85a, Rabbi entrusted R' Yose son of R' Elazar son of R' Shimon—see his entry—to R' Shimon ben Issi—in Yalkut Mishlei, chapter 11, ben Yose—ben Lakunya, “his mother's sister.” It should read “his mother's brother,” as in Ein Yaakov, so that he would teach him Torah; see his entry. This suggests that R' Elazar son of R' Shimon married a daughter of R' Yose ben Lakunya. Thus R' Elazar's wife was R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya's sister, and R' Yose son of R' Elazar was entrusted to R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya, his mother's brother. Alternatively, it must be emended to “his mother's father.” But I labored and found in Zohar, Bereshit, at 25, Sulzbach edition [all following Zohar locators provisional and uncollated], 5c: R' Elazar son of R' Shimon went to see R' Yose son of R' Shimon ben Lakunya, with R' Abba. There, 6c: when he reached R' Yose son of R' Shimon ben Lakunya's house. In Zohar, Noah 46a, in that edition: R' Elazar went to R' Yose son of R' Shimon ben Lakunya, his father-in-law. Likewise Zohar, Balak, end of 356. In Zohar, Kedoshim, at 113: R' Elazar was going to visit (R' Yose), R' Shimon (son of R' Shimon) ben Lakunya, and R' Hiyya and R' Yose were with him; it is marked in a circle in that Zohar edition. In Zohar, Devarim, at 488 [the checked verbal parallel is in Balak 6:63]: R' Elazar son of R' Shimon wished to visit R' Yose son of R' Shimon ben Lakunya, his father-in-law, and R' Abba and R' Yose (and R' Hiyya) went with him. Thus it is explicit that R' Yose ben Lakunya was his father-in-law, not R' Shimon son of R' Yose ben Lakunya. Perhaps the intention of the foregoing Bavli, Jerusalem Talmud, and Rabbah—that he went to R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya, his father-in-law—is that R' Yose was his father-in-law, but that is strained. Yet the wording in all those Zohar passages, “R' Yose son of R' Shimon ben Lakunya,” cannot be found as R' Yose son of R' Shimon ben Lakunya, for R' Yose was ben Lakunya.

See Arukh, entry Atzvata: in Vayehi be-Shallah Par'oh, R' Elazar ben Shammua went to his father-in-law R' Shimon ben Yohai Lakunya. He slaughtered an ox for him, baked one atzva, and opened a jar of wine for him. End of quotation. I did not find it in Rabbah or Yelammedenu. In any case there is a scribal error: it should read R' Elazar son of R' Shimon went to R' Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya.
